This is my sorghum plot here in the North East, where the rains only come once and the soil is tired from seasons past. I will put some NPK and a top-dress of urea, but not too much because the prices at the agro-dealer are high this year — maybe around 35 kg of nitrogen per hectare, plus manure from my animals to help the soil hold water. I will plant the local sorghum seed I saved from last year since it handles our dry spells well, and I don't see the need for pesticide on sorghum. My wife, my older children and I will do most of the work, but at weeding time and harvest I will call some young men from the village to help for a few days.
